body:
# Yamunā, spelled the way the sources wrote it
There is a version of this name the early internet had to settle for: *yamuna*. This is the file on how **Yamunā** replaced it.

Yamunā's myths bind the solar and the pastoral: the sun's daughter flowing through the cowherd's land, purifying and purified by the god who plays in her. Born of Sūrya and Saṃjñā, twin sister of Yama — death and the river as siblings, the tradition's quiet pairing.  The Purāṇas rank her beside Gaṅgā in holiness and ahead in intimacy: if Gaṅgā is the mother, Yamunā is the beloved — the river whose water Kṛṣṇa drank as a child and blessed as a god, making her, alone of rivers, "the co-wife of the Lord.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Yamunā
- **ASCII form:** yamuna
- **Meaning:** "The Twin River — daughter of Sūrya, twin of Yama, Kṛṣṇa's beloved water"
- **Domain of influence:** Sacred River, Twin of Yama
- **Pantheon:** Sanskrit
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** यमुना
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 268 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

Strip **Yamunā** to *yamuna* and one piece of evidence vanishes:

- **a → ā** — Long vowel: the vowel length the ASCII form cannot show.

A reader who knows the marks hears the name correctly on the first try. A reader who never sees them never gets the chance.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Yamunā** lives at [/sites/yamuna/](/sites/yamuna/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/yamuna/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/yamuna/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/yamuna/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Yamunā** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Environmental & Climate Services** — Delhi's stretch of her is among the world's most polluted urban rivers; her cleanup is India's restoration test case.
- **Freshwater & Hydrology** — India’s second great river-goddess; the Yamunā’s dark-blue water is Kṛṣṇa’s own — a working river revered as divine.
- **Love, Dating & Relationships** — Kṛṣṇa's beloved, “co-wife of the Lord”; the rāsa-līlā romance plays out on her banks.

The mapping is conservative on purpose: only resonances that can be argued aloud. The rest of the atlas follows the same rule, industry by industry.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Sanskrit tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Rig Veda](/texts/rig-veda/) and [Ramayana](/texts/ramayana/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.

This is one of 271 Restoration Files — a second dispatch from every flagship temple in the fleet. The temple's [first dispatch](/sites/yamuna/blog/) tells the founding story of the name; the [blog index](/blog/) holds the whole archive.
